summary: Intermittent SAML assertions for service-account -> internal-analytics fail with 403 \"insufficient_scope\" when device-trust header is stripped
description: Issue summary: Internal service integrations using ephemeral service-account tokens to call internal-analytics began receiving intermittent 403 responses with an \"insufficient_scope\" message during SAML assertion exchange. Impact: Scheduled data ingestion jobs and a small set of internal dashboards started failing between 08:12 and 11:40 UTC; affected jobs retried and caused increased queue backpressure but no customer-facing outage. Environment: prod cluster, internal-analytics (console) behind Okta SAML app, device-trust policy enforced company-wide for interactive logins. Initial hypothesis: device-trust enforcement or a malformed header on the proxy was stripping a required attribute from the SAML assertion used by service accounts, causing RBAC role mapping to drop required groups.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Generate service-account ephemeral token via internal service-token broker (used by data pipelines)
2) Exchange token for SAML assertion with Okta SAML app configured for internal-analytics
3) POST assertion to internal-analytics SAML endpoint via service proxy (simulates pipeline path)
4) Observe 403 response with body: {\"error\": \"insufficient_scope\", \"details\": \"missing_group:internal_analytics_viewer\"} intermittently (approx 3/10 attempts in observed window)
5) Re-run the flow from the host that bypasses the proxy and observe success consistently
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:05 (Luis): Customer (internal) ticket filed after dashboard failures; attached example request/response and job IDs

2026-03-10 09:30 (Amira): Pulled Okta System Logs for SAML app 'internal-analytics' for the 08:00-12:00 UTC window. Noted SAML responses with missing 'groups' attribute correlate to requests routed through api-proxy-3 (hosted in us-east).

2026-03-10 10:00 (SRE): Captured tcpdump on api-proxy-3. Found that an internal security sidecar (device-trust injector) inserted X-Device-Trust header for interactive flows but occasionally returned an empty header for service-to-service requests, which triggered Okta's attribute filter in our SAML app to drop the 'groups' claim.

2026-03-10 10:45 (Identity): Reviewed Okta SAML attribute mapping. Mapping rule required presence of X-Device-Trust (non-empty) to include SCIM groups for assertion. Service tokens that hit the proxy with an empty header caused the mapping to evaluate false and omit group claims.

2026-03-10 11:10 (Infra): Reproduced locally by replaying a service token exchange through the proxy with the sidecar configured to return an empty X-Device-Trust header. Confirmed SAML assertion lacked groups and internal-analytics returned 403 insufficient_scope.

2026-03-11 02:00 (Amira): Cross-checked proxy rollout history and noted a sidecar config change deployed 2026-03-09 23:50 that tightened header defaults; suspect that change caused unexpected empty-value behavior for non-interactive flows.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:40 - Luis Moreno (Reporter): 'Posting example job IDs: pipeline-analytics-8472 failing at 3rd retry. Attached HTTP traces.'
2026-03-10 10:20 - SRE (Kyle Patel): 'Seeing correlation between proxy host api-proxy-3 and the failures. Will place host in maintenance pool and route traffic to api-proxy-1/2 for mitigation.'

2026-03-10 11:05 - Identity (Maya Singh): 'Okta mapping currently uses expression: if(X-Device-Trust != \"\") then include groups. That conditional explains missing groups when header exists but is empty. Recommend mapping change or ensure proxy never emits empty header for service tokens.'

2026-03-10 11:45 - Amira Chen (Assignee): 'Mitigation: added temporary rule in Okta to include groups for SAML assertions originating from our service-account issuer (service-token-broker) regardless of device-trust header. Rollout completed at 11:30 UTC, validated by re-running failing pipeline - success.'

2026-03-11 08:15 - Infra (Jamal Ortiz): 'Root cause confirmed: sidecar config defaulted an empty X-Device-Trust value for non-browser flows after config change. Created PR to change default behavior and add a test that ensures non-interactive flows do not inject empty headers.'

2026-03-12 14:00 - Amira Chen: 'Resolution deployed: Okta mapping updated to check issuer and fall back to issuer-based group inclusion; sidecar default fixed and rolled back to previous behavior on api-proxy fleet. Closing incident after 48h stable verification.'
resolution: Implemented two-step fix: 1) Short-term Okta mapping patch to include SCIM groups for assertions from our service-token-broker issuer (rolled at 11:30 UTC) to immediately stop 403s. 2) Long-term fix in infra: patched sidecar behavior to never emit empty X-Device-Trust header for non-interactive flows and added unit/integration tests; rolled to prod api-proxy fleet 2026-03-11 03:20. Verified by re-running failing jobs and observing normal success rates. No further 403s observed in 48h monitoring window.
post_mortem_actions: Add CI test to infra that asserts proxy sidecar does not inject empty X-Device-Trust for service-to-service requests
Update Identity Runbook: include guidance for mapping rules that should not depend solely on device-trust header for non-interactive SAML assertions
Add monitoring alert when >1% of SAML assertions for a given app are missing 'groups' attribute in a 5m window
Schedule follow-up audit of all Okta SAML apps to search for mapping rules that could be affected by empty headers
